name: rock-fragmenter-breaking
description: Chapter 5/2 (#484), superseded by #552's self-dispatching hauling/fragmenting: an undercharged blast leaves an oversized boulder that auto-dispatch routes to a crewed rock_fragmenter (fragment_debris PendingAction) rather than a debris_hauler (haul_debris) -- no player command or button picks which vehicle goes where any more, and there is no rejection to test either, since an oversized fragment simply never spawns a haul_debris action in the first place. A resulting sub-fragment is then hauled and stored automatically once a freight_warehouse exists. Buy/driver-assign purchases still go through real Vehicles-panel clicks; the break/haul actions themselves are proven by ticking forward and reading the automatic outcome.

steps.description: #553: cash bumped from $100,000 to $150,000 to cover the driller/drill_rig this file now needs (see below) on top of the original driver/debris_hauler/driver/rock_fragmenter/freight_warehouse shopping list.

#553: drill_hole is now a queued, vehicle-gated action -- a driller physically drives a drill_rig to each hole -- so this file (which pre-#553 never needed any roster before the driver/fragmenter dance below) now needs one first. Employee #1; the debris_hauler driver hired later becomes #2, and the rock_fragmenter driver #3, one slot later than this file's pre-#553 numbering.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants blasting at Rookie (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION), but no role starts with driving.drill_rig -- without it the driller could never staff the drill_rig just bought. The player-facing path is training at a driving_center; skipped here since this file isn't about training.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:5 depth:6 start:18,19 diameter:0.089
steps.description: The grid tool's spacing stepper defaults to 3m (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts); two increment clicks raise it to 5 before dragging, so the (18,19)-(23,24) rectangle (5x5) computes the declared 2x2 instead of the default-spacing 3x3 (issue #479 follow-up, Finding #4). depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. #553: confirming the grid queues 4 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 4 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none are drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm. diameter:0.089 added for the same reason interaction mode never needed it stated: the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission alone was keeping the drill_rig busy (and paying fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks in command mode that the real click's grid never spent, a $54 divergence on every downstream cash checkpoint below. Confirmed exact: adding the real default here reproduces interaction mode's own $108,622/$107,822/$82,822 figures precisely.

expect.note: 2 rows x 2 cols = 4 holes ordered (ghosts), none drilled yet (#553)

steps.description: #553: drain the ordered plan — the driller/drill_rig lands all 4 holes well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 18 for H4).

expect.note: All 4 holes have landed — none lost, none left ordered forever.

a fired blast clears the plan back to zero; undercharged 2kg boomite at wide 5m spacing leaves oversized boulders on the ground (verified via the fragments step below), setting up the fragmenter's real job

steps.description: Undercharged 2kg boomite at wide 5m spacing (mirrors blast-undercharge.json) reliably leaves a couple of oversized fragments (volume > OVERSIZED_FRAGMENT_THRESHOLD) among the ground fragments — this step's output exposes their ids. Interaction mode's blast step above also dismisses the Blast Report modal (data-action="report-close") that the blast command opens — otherwise its .bs-confirm-overlay backdrop blocks every later click (#484's original scenario had the same gap; command mode never surfaced it since there's no DOM to click against).
Employee #2 (#553: #1 is now the driller hired at the top of this file) — will be crewed onto the debris_hauler.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`.
Opens the Vehicles panel via a real UI click so every later buy/driver/haul/break button click below targets a panel that is already on-screen (#411 pattern).

Vehicle #2 (#553: #1 was the drill_rig bought at the top of this file, destroyed sitting inside its own hole's blast radius — see the blast step above) — a real click on the tier-1 debris_hauler buy button. Click is the sole purchase action in interaction mode (the top-level `command` covers command mode) — combining both double-buys (#484).

expect.note: debris_hauler tier-1 purchaseCost = 25000 (balance.ts); vehicleCount is 1, not 2, because the blast above destroyed vehicle #1 (the drill_rig)

steps.description: Only one licensed (driving.truck) crew member is eligible, so the driver <select> already defaults to employee #2 (#553's driller renumbering) — the assign button click alone boards them.
Lets the driver walk to and board the hauler.

#552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle haul 1 fragment:0' rejection step -- there is no haul attempt to refuse any more, since an oversized fragment never spawns a haul_debris PendingAction in the first place (syncHaulDispatch routes it to fragment_debris instead). No freight_warehouse exists yet at this point in the file either way, so nothing can be delivered regardless.

expect.note: no active freight_warehouse exists yet, so storedMassKg staying 0 holds regardless of what auto-dispatch attempts

steps.description: Employee #3 (#553: #1 is now the driller, #2 the debris_hauler driver) — will be crewed onto the rock_fragmenter.

expect.note: HIRING_COSTS.driver = 800 plus salary/maintenance drained by the tick 10 above. Not an exact-cash check: unlike a hire with no ticks in between, new_game runs with isPaused:false by default, so interaction mode's real wall-clock during the tick 10 step's click round-trip advances the sim beyond exactly 10 ticks — command mode has no such drift (no timers, only explicit tick N). decreased is the only cross-mode-robust check here.

steps.description: Unlike the driving.truck bootstrap above, this one grants a licence from nothing: employee #3 was hired as a driver (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION driving.truck only), and driving.excavator belongs to no hiring role at all -- the real path is training at a driving_center (see employee-training.json's own conversion of that exact flow). Left as a test-only bootstrap since this file's focus is the rock_fragmenter break/haul flow, not re-proving excavator licensing.

Vehicle #3 (#553: #1 was the drill_rig, destroyed by the blast; #2 is the debris_hauler) — a real click on the tier-1 rock_fragmenter buy button. Click is the sole purchase action in interaction mode (the top-level `command` covers command mode) — combining both double-buys (#484).

expect.note: rock_fragmenter tier-1 purchaseCost = 32000 (balance.ts) — decreased, not an exact value, since this step's baseline (hire2's real cash) already carries the previous step's real-time drift (see hire2's note)

steps.description: Lets the second driver walk to and board the rock_fragmenter.

#552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle break 2 fragment:60' step and its .bs-vehicle-break-btn click -- once the rock_fragmenter and its licensed driver exist, the oversized boulder's own fragment_debris PendingAction is claimed and driven to automatically, with no player command or button naming which boulder. The following tick-30 padding step lets the drive-and-break cycle actually finish.
Padding: the fragmenter drives to the boulder's approach cell and breaks it on arrival.

expect.note: 50 ticks of salary/maintenance drain since the last checkpoint — decreased, not an exact value; interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (isPaused:false by default, no explicit pause in this file) advances the sim beyond exactly N ticks during every click round-trip, a drift command mode's headless tick N can't reproduce

steps.description: #553: idempotent — a no-op ('No pending event or invalid option.') when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired mid-tick-block (sandbox-measured: a Book Club event fires around here on seed 42). A bare `tick` refuses outright while an event is pending, so skipping this defensively stalls every tick step after it.
Fragment #1 should now be gone from logistics, replaced by haulable sub-fragments (each under OVERSIZED_FRAGMENT_THRESHOLD) whose total volume matches the original boulder.

expect.note: freight_warehouse T1 constructionCost = 15000 (balance.ts) — decreased, not an exact value, since this step's baseline already carries the tick 30 step's real-time drift (see that step's note)

steps.description: #552: replaces the old manual 'vehicle haul 1 fragment:56' step and its .bs-vehicle-haul-btn click -- one of the sub-fragments the automatic break above produced is on_ground and non-oversized, so it already has its own haul_debris PendingAction; the idle debris_hauler's driver claims and delivers it with no player command or button naming which fragment. The following tick-30 padding step lets the drive-load-deliver cycle actually finish.
Padding: the hauler drives to the piece, loads it, drives to the warehouse, and delivers it.

expect.note: the file's own long-standing TODO ('Final assertion point: logistics.storedMassKg must have grown') finally has a real check — storedMassKg was 0 through the whole file until this delivery (verified: the earlier haul-refused step already proved that), so 'increased' here is the genuine proof the sub-fragment was hauled and stored, not just that the button clicked. Not an exact storedMassKg value: interaction mode's real wall-clock ticking (isPaused:false by default) can extend this 'tick 30' step's effective duration enough for the hauler to complete more than one round trip, so the exact delivered mass isn't guaranteed identical to command mode's — increased is the cross-mode-robust proof.

steps.description: Final assertion point: logistics.storedMassKg must have grown by exactly the hauled piece's mass — checked on the tick 30 step above (the state the delivery actually lands in), since command mode's `before`/`after` capture is per-step and this step's own command is a pure read with nothing left to change.
